program.description: NJ 211 is a statewide nonprofit whose 211 call centre operates 24 hours a day for New Jersey residents facing a crisis or a disaster. It maintains a directory of more than 6,300 government and nonprofit programmes, continually updated by curators, which its specialists use when assisting callers and which residents can search themselves. NJ 211 also serves as the State's Home Energy Assistance Hotline and Homeless Hotline, and reaches residents by phone, chat, text and web.
program.plain_language_summary: Dial 2-1-1 any time, day or night, and a real person in New Jersey will help you find food, housing, utility help, childcare and more. You can also search their directory online or reach them by text or chat.

sources.title: About NJ 211
sources.excerpt:
NJ 211 is a statewide nonprofit organization renowned for its 211 call center that operates 24 hours a day for New Jersey’s residents facing a crisis or dealing with a disaster. We maintain a robust and comprehensive directory of over 6,300 government and nonprofit programs, which is continually updated by a team of curators to ensure the most up-to-date information on programs. The directory is used by our specialists when assisting callers and can also found on our website for easy use by residents.
Yet it’s our one-to-one, human-centered approach to service delivery that is our trademark. We take great pride in personally interacting with residents and the agencies that serve them. When people dial 211, they reach someone who will listen carefully and guide them to the health and human services resources and services they need

program.description: The Middlesex County Board of Social Services is the County Social Service Agency that takes and decides applications for New Jersey's means-tested programmes for Middlesex County residents, including NJ SNAP, Work First New Jersey cash assistance, emergency assistance and Medicaid. Its office is at 181 How Lane in New Brunswick and it is open 8:30 AM to 4:15 PM Monday to Friday.
program.plain_language_summary: If you live in Middlesex County, this is the county office that actually decides your SNAP, cash assistance and Medicaid applications. You can go in person to 181 How Lane in New Brunswick, or call them with questions about an application.
